business: The Aldera, magnesium bisglycinate in daily sachets
why_not: I already take Toplux and reorder when it runs out, and $29.99 is more than Toplux or Goli for a month. I'm not switching a routine that works for something I've never heard of.
I already have my supplement and I reorder it when it runs out, so I am not looking for a new one. Two capsules a day is still capsules, and the sachet does not change that for me.

I don't take supplements unless a doctor tells me to, and nobody has told me I'm low on magnesium. I can get a bottle of magnesium at a drugstore for under $15, so $30 a month for the same thing in a foil packet isn't worth it to me.
I already take magnesium at night at home, and I have a drawer of half-used supplement bottles. I don't need it to go, and I'm not buying another one without a doctor telling me to.
$29.99 is more than Toplux or Goli and those last longer. The sachet idea fits my gym bag, but I'm not paying a premium for it when I could get magnesium for a lot less.
I already take Toplux and reorder it. $29.99 is more than Toplux ($23) or Goli ($19) and those last longer, and I have a drawer of half-used bottles already.

Thirty foil sachets a month is a lot of trash for something I can get in a bottle, and I already compare magnesium by price per day. The lab report and the guarantee are nice, but they don't beat a bottle that costs less.
why_yes: Batch lab reports on the page and behind the QR code are what I check before buying anything, and the sachets are handy when I travel twice a month. At the $24.99 launch price I would try one box, not two.

The named lab and the per-batch report would normally win me over, and at $24.99 the launch box works out to about 83 cents a day, which I can live with. I would try one box, not two, and only because the empty-box guarantee means I am not stuck with another half-used bottle in the drawer.

My doctor said my magnesium could be low and I always forget pills at home, so a sachet I can toss in my bag is what I'd actually take. The lab report and the money-back thing make me OK trying one box at the $24.99 price.

The sachet thing is actually handy, I can throw one in my gym bag and not think about it, and the lab report plus money-back thing makes it low risk at $24.99. I'd grab one box on impulse if a creator I follow showed it, but I wouldn't commit to a second yet.

My doctor said my magnesium could be low, so I actually have a reason, and $24.99 for the first box with a money-back guarantee is a risk I can take once. At $29.99 I would probably just grab a cheaper bottle.
flip: My doctor telling me my magnesium is low and recommending it. Even then it would have to be close to drugstore price.
